title: A rename leaves the old number on part sale lines that hold the part
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test with 5 on hand.
  • Create an open part sale for this test, part sale A, with a line holding 1 of part A picked from stock.
  • Create a part sale for this test, part sale B, with a line holding 1 of part A picked from stock, and invoice it so it is completed.
  • Use a new part number that no part and no Part Library entry has yet, and that does not contain part A's number.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part A row.
  3. Replace the Part Number with the new number.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Click Part Sales in the left menu.
  6. Open part sale A.
  7. Click Part Sales in the left menu.
  8. Open part sale B.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 3:

  • Part Number shows the new number.

Step 4:

  • The rename is saved, the window closes and part A's row shows the new number.

Step 5:

  • The Part Sales list opens.

Step 6:

  • Part sale A, still open, shows its line for part A with the old number: a part already on a part sale line keeps the number it was added with.

Step 7:

  • The Part Sales list opens.

Step 8:

  • Part sale B, completed, also shows its line for part A with the old number.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S13-R19e: “A part already received onto a work order or part sale line, open or not, keeps the number it was added with. Only a part request that is not yet received or returned takes the new number (S13-R19).”
  • Story 13, context note: “Context note: S13-R19 matters because those records hold their own copy of the number and find the part by it later. Records already completed, such as received purchase order lines, completed returns and past work orders and invoices, keep the number they were written with. The Inventory list, Part History, Parts Velocity and today's Inventory Value show the new number. Inventory Value run for a date before the rename shows the number as it was on that date.”

From: Product's answers to questions 13 to 27 (Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, Google Doc https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pkAPGqWVTdtYorNN4SVNl9HkHxuuB9czro_y2DbUeEM/edit, saved word for word in full-pass-2026-10-27/ANSWERS-13-27-2026-10-27.md), read 28 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, answer 26: “It depends on the line. A part already received onto a work order or part sale line keeps the number it was added with. A part request not yet received or returned takes the new number (S13-R19e).”
